creator: quietkitchen
title: Cardamom Buns
description: Grind the cardamom yourself. It is the whole difference between these and a plain sweet bun.
steps: Grind the cardamom seeds yourself; pre-ground is a different, duller spice.
Warm the milk to blood heat, stir in the yeast and a spoon of the sugar, and leave 10 minutes.
Work the flour, salt, remaining sugar and half the cardamom into the milk to a soft dough.
Knead 10 minutes, then work in the butter a lump at a time until glossy.
Prove until doubled, about an hour, then roll out and spread with the rest of the butter and cardamom.
Fold, cut into strips, twist each one into a knot and prove 40 minutes more.
Brush with egg, scatter pearl sugar, and bake at 425F for 12 minutes until deep gold.

creator: quietkitchen
title: Sourdough Loaf
description: Overnight in the fridge does more for the flavour than anything you can do on the day.
steps: Feed the starter 6 hours ahead; it should double and smell of yoghurt, not vinegar.
Mix the flours and water and leave 45 minutes so the flour hydrates.
Work in the starter and salt, then fold the dough over itself four times at half-hour intervals.
Leave to rise 4 hours at room temperature, until risen by half and domed.
Shape into a tight round, seam down in a floured banneton, and refrigerate overnight.
Bake from cold in a lidded pot at 475F for 20 minutes, then 25 minutes uncovered.
Cool completely before cutting; a warm loaf tears rather than slices.

creator: quietkitchen
title: Spelt Kifli
description: Spelt takes less kneading than wheat and goes slack if you push it. Stop while it still springs back.
steps: Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm milk and leave until it foams.
Mix in the spelt flour, salt and butter, and knead to a soft dough — spelt needs a lighter hand than wheat.
Prove an hour, then roll into a large circle and cut it into twelve wedges.
Roll each wedge from the wide end to the point, and curve it into a crescent.
Prove 30 minutes on the tray, brush with egg and scatter the sesame.
Bake at 400F for 18 minutes until the tops are deep gold.

creator: quietkitchen
title: Gougeres
description: Do not open the oven. They rise on steam, and steam leaves the moment you look.
steps: Bring the water, butter and salt to a rolling boil.
Tip in all the flour at once and beat hard until it leaves the side of the pan.
Cool for five minutes, or the eggs will scramble on contact.
Beat the eggs in one at a time; the paste should fall from the spoon in a thick ribbon.
Fold through most of the cheese and the nutmeg.
Pipe walnut-sized mounds, top with the rest of the cheese, and bake at 400F for 25 minutes.
Do not open the oven before 20 minutes or they will sink.

creator: quietkitchen
title: Onigiri
description: Wet, salted hands. It seasons the rice and it is the only way it will not stick to you instead.
ingredients: rinsed until the water runs clear
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then cook it and let it stand 10 minutes covered.
Beat the eggs with a splash of soy and cook them flat in a wide pan, then cut into squares.
Wet your hands and salt them; the salt seasons the rice and stops it sticking.
Press a handful of warm rice into a triangle, lay the egg and pork on top, and press a second layer over.
Wrap a strip of nori around the base of each.
Eat within the day; refrigerated rice goes hard and no amount of warming brings it back.

creator: quietkitchen
title: Asparagus Soup
description: The woody ends make the stock. Snap them off, simmer them, and throw them out afterwards.
steps: Snap the woody ends off the asparagus and simmer them in the stock for 15 minutes, then strain them out.
Cut the tips off and set them aside; chop the rest.
Soften the onion in the butter without colouring it.
Add the chopped stalks and the asparagus stock and simmer 12 minutes.
Blend until completely smooth, then pass it through a sieve — asparagus keeps its threads otherwise.
Stir in the cream, warm through without boiling, and sharpen with lemon.
Blanch the tips for 2 minutes and drop them into each bowl.

creator: quietkitchen
title: Koshary
description: The fried onions are not a garnish. Give them the twenty minutes they need and do the rest around them.
steps: Fry the onions in batches until dark brown and crisp, and drain them on paper. This takes 20 minutes and is the dish.
Simmer the lentils until tender but whole, about 20 minutes, and drain.
Cook the rice and the pasta separately so neither goes to mush.
For the sauce, fry the garlic and cumin in a spoon of the onion oil, add the tomatoes and vinegar, and simmer 15 minutes.
Layer rice, lentils, pasta and chickpeas in a wide dish.
Pour the hot sauce over and pile the fried onions on top at the very last moment.

creator: quietkitchen
title: Ajiaco
description: Two kinds of potato, and they are doing different jobs: one dissolves to thicken it, one stays whole.
steps: Simmer the chicken with the onion and garlic in water to cover for 35 minutes, then lift it out and shred it.
Add the floury potatoes to the broth and let them collapse completely — that is what thickens it.
Add the waxy potatoes and the corn and cook 20 minutes more, until the waxy ones hold but give.
Stir the guascas in for the last 5 minutes only; longer and they turn bitter.
Return the chicken and season.
Serve with the cream, capers and avocado on the side, for each person to add.

creator: quietkitchen
title: Apple Cake with Vanilla Ice Cream
description: Warm, not hot. Straight from the oven the cake is too loose to hold the ice cream up.
steps: Use a firm apple that holds its shape; a soft one turns to sauce and wets the crumb.
Cream the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and cinnamon.
Spread into a lined tin and press the apple slices in, standing them on edge.
Bake at 350F for 45 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Serve warm rather than hot, with the ice cream going soft against it.

creator: quietkitchen
title: Canneles
description: The batter has to rest a day. Rushed, they rise like a souffle and collapse into a pancake.
steps: Warm the milk with the butter and the split vanilla pod, then take it off the heat and leave it to infuse.
Whisk the yolks, whole egg and sugar, then the flour and salt, to a smooth batter.
Pour the warm milk in slowly, whisking — all at once and the egg cooks into threads.
Strain, cover, and rest in the fridge for 24 hours. This is not optional; an unrested batter rises and collapses.
Brush the moulds thickly with melted butter and chill them until set.
Fill to just below the rim and bake at 475F for 15 minutes, then 375F for 40 minutes.
They should be almost black outside and custardy within. Turn them out at once or they steam and soften.
